defects.title: The subplot grid is transposed for perScreen = [nY, nX]
defects.trigger: perScreen = [1 2] (documented as [nY, nX], one row of two plots)

notes: independent review T027/T028: finding confirmed in MATLAB (R2025a, 2026-11-17). Reproduction: model1 = createModel({'r1','r2'},{'r1','r2'},{'A -> B','B -> C'}); modelBack = createModel({'r1','r2'},{'r1','r2'},{'A <=> B','B -> C'}); modelBack.lb(1) = -10; modelBack.ub(1) = 0; model2 = convertToIrreversible(modelBack) (rxns r1_r, r2); rng(1); s1 = rand(2,50); s2 = rand(2,50); plotSampleHist({'r1','r2'},{s1,s2},{model1,model2},5) -> one subplot only ('Flux of r2'); plotSampleHist({'r1'},{s1,s2},{model1,model2},5) -> 'Index exceeds array bounds.' at line 128 (figure left open); plotSampleHist({'r1_x'},{s1},{model1},5) -> the same at line 128; findRxnIDs(model1,'zz') -> 0. Severity: wrong-result by the review rule (handling code that is never reached, lines 130-138 and 158-165, states the intent to plot the negated samples of <rxn>_r; lines 91-106 drop the reaction first and findRxnIDs never returns empty). The index error is a second entry, error: rxnNames taken from one model with the models in a cell is the header's own example (line 37), and a call where no requested reaction is in every model stops instead of reaching the 'Reaction does not exist' warning of line 137. The cosmetic grid entry (line 171) is kept. Test converted to the quarantine layout (the former coverage exemption 'dead code' for lines 131-138/159-164 is now the wrong-result entry). Reach: both defects depend on the model contents (a model holding a requested reaction only as <rxn>_r; no requested reaction common to all models), not on a call form recognisable in calling code, so every call reaches them. src callers of plotSampleHist: none (grep 'plotSampleHist(' in src finds only the function). cobraSmooth is called for every input (extra edge, as in wave 17).
confirmed_by: lead (review T027/T028; l.91-106 drop reactions missing from a model before the <rxn>_r handling at l.130-138/158-165 can run; writer's MATLAB reproduction with a convertToIrreversible model)

defects.title: The lung of a whole-body model keeps the reference weight instead of the lung polynomial
defects.trigger: calcOrganFract(model, struct('sex', 'male', 'bodyWeight', 100, 'CardiacOutput', 5360, 'OrgansWeights', {{}})) for a model with the reaction Lung_biomass_maintenance, e.g. struct('rxns', {{'Lung_biomass_maintenance'}}) or the rxns of the shipped Harvey_1_03d (test/models/mat), whose only lung reaction is Lung_biomass_maintenance (no reaction starts with Lungs_)
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-17) the polynomials name the lung 'Lungs' (lines 70 and 88) while the whole-body models and the reference table name it 'Lung' (OrganLists.m, getOrganWeightFraction), so lines 174-188 treat the model's Lung as an organ without polynomial: the output lists both 'Lungs' (1079.05 g at 70 kg, 1405.00 g at 100 kg) and 'Lung' (536 g at every body weight, the reference man's value); the same with the Harvey reactions at 100 kg
defects.expected: the model's lung weighted by the lung polynomial of Table 3 (the header, lines 4-8, and the comment of lines 167-171 keep only organs not given there constant), listed once

notes: independent review T027/T028: finding confirmed in MATLAB (R2025a, 2026-11-17). Naming in the shipped data the documented inputs use: the shipped whole-body model test/models/mat/Harvey_1_03d.mat (variable male, 81094 reactions) has the reaction Lung_biomass_maintenance and no reaction starting with Lungs_; OrganLists.m line 7 lists 'Lung'; the reference table read by getOrganWeightFraction (Numbers_organWeightData_fromxls_16_01_29_OrganWeigths.mat) names it 'Lung'; only calcOrganFract lines 70 and 88 say 'Lungs'. Reproduction: IP = struct('sex','male','bodyWeight',70,'CardiacOutput',5360,'OrgansWeights',{{}}); [organs, W] = calcOrganFract(struct('rxns',{{'Lung_biomass_maintenance'}}), IP) -> Lungs 1079.05 g, Lung 536 g; with bodyWeight 100 -> Lungs 1405.00 g, Lung 536 g; calcOrganFract(struct('rxns',{Harvey.rxns}), IP) at 100 kg gives the same two entries. Of the 14 male polynomial organs only Lungs, Blood and Thymus have no <Organ>_biomass_maintenance reaction in Harvey (Blood is represented by its cell types, Thymus is not modelled), so the lung is the one mis-weighted organ. Severity wrong-result (contradicts the header, lines 4-8, and the comment of lines 167-171). The former test asserted Lung = 536 g as expected; converted to the quarantine layout. Reach: every call form with a whole-body model (they all carry Lung_biomass_maintenance); not confined to a recognisable call form. src callers: src/analysis/persephone/persWBM.m line 817 (passes organs and fractions on to adjustWholeBodyRxnCoeff; already BLOCKED), src/analysis/wholeBody/PSCMToolbox/BMRcalculations/perform_BMR_newData.m lines 113 and 307 and perform_sensi_BMR_all.m line 135 (scripts, EXCLUDED).
confirmed_by: lead (review T027/T028; l.70/88 name 'Lungs' while Harvey_1_03d, OrganLists and the reference table name 'Lung'; writer's MATLAB reproduction: Lung stays at 536 g at any weight)

notes: independent review T027/T028: finding confirmed in MATLAB (R2025a, 2026-11-17). defects.title: Each dependent metabolite is reported as dependent on itself
defects.trigger: the model returned by checkRankFR for fm = createModel({'R1'; 'R2'; 'R3'; 'R4'}, {'R1'; 'R2'; 'R3'; 'R4'}, {'A + C -> E'; 'E -> A + D'; 'B + D -> G'; 'G -> B + C'}) with lb = -1000, ub = 1000 and SIntRxnBool, SIntMetBool, SConsistentRxnBool, SConsistentMetBool all true; printFRdependencies(fmOut). checkRankFR itself stops at its line 541 on this machine (method.solver 'gurobi5' and method.interface 'solveCobraLP' are hard-coded at its lines 534-535), so the fields were produced by a copy of checkRankFR with only those two names changed to 'gurobi' and 'SDCCO'
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-17) checkRankFR gives rankFR = 5, FRdrows = D[c], FRW = [A:1, B:1, C:-1, D:-1] (lines 636-655 of checkRankFR put -1 at the dependent row) and the report prints 'D[c] is dependent on: A[c] and B[c] and C[c] and D[c].' (lines 38 and 97 list every nonzero FRW column, the dependent row included); the same for two copies of the module (C[c] and Cx[c] each listed as dependent on themselves)
defects.expected: 'D[c] is dependent on: A[c] and B[c] and C[c].' (the documented FRW expresses dependent rows as combinations of independent rows)

defects.title: Dependent rows are counted and displayed among the independent rows
defects.trigger: the same checkRankFR output as the entry above; printFRdependencies(fmOut)
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-17) FRwrows of checkRankFR (its line 641) holds every nonzero FRW column, so wR = A, B, C, D includes the dependent row D; the report prints 'FR subset of dimension 5 x 4, of rank 3.', '4 independent rows:' (D among them) and '1 dependent rows:' (D again): row D appears twice in FRdisplay (lines 74 and 130). With two copies of the module: '10 x 8', '8 independent rows:', '2 dependent rows:'
defects.expected: 3 independent rows (A, B, C) and 1 dependent row (D), a 4-row submatrix

notes: independent review T027/T028: finding confirmed with the checkRankFR algorithm (R2025a, 2026-11-17). checkRankFR cannot run unchanged: without SConsistentMetBool/SConsistentRxnBool it stops at line 163 in checkStoichiometricConsistency ('unregognised method.interface = solveCobraLP', line 346), and with them always at line 541 (changeCobraSolver: 'The solver gurobi5 is not available to the COBRA Toolbox on your machine.'), since lines 534-535 hard-code method.interface 'solveCobraLP' and method.solver 'gurobi5'. The FR fields were therefore produced by a copy of checkRankFR in the scratch folder with only those names changed to 'SDCCO' and 'gurobi' (lines 586-656, which build FRdrows, FRW and FRwrows, unchanged), solver gurobi. Reproduction: fm = createModel({'R1';'R2';'R3';'R4'},{'R1';'R2';'R3';'R4'},{'A + C -> E';'E -> A + D';'B + D -> G';'G -> B + C'}); fm.lb(:) = -1000; fm.ub(:) = 1000; fm.SIntRxnBool = true(4,1); fm.SIntMetBool = true(6,1); fm.SConsistentRxnBool = true(4,1); fm.SConsistentMetBool = true(6,1); [~,~,~,~,fmOut] = checkRankFR(fm,0) -> rankFR 5, FRdrows D[c], FRwrows A,B,C,D, FRW = [A:1 B:1 C:-1 D:-1]; printFRdependencies(fmOut) prints 'D[c] is dependent on: A[c] and B[c] and C[c] and D[c].', 'FR subset of dimension 5 x 4, of rank 3.', '4 independent rows:' (D among them) and '1 dependent rows:' (D again). Two copies of the module (8 reactions): deficiency 2, FRp tail [5 6] (C[c], Cx[c]), each listed as dependent on itself, '10 x 8', '8 independent rows:'. The reviewer's row-order mislabel (FRW rows in LUSOL pivot order vs the sorted find(FRdrows)) was not reproduced: the pivot tail was ascending in both probes; it stays possible in principle and is not recorded. Severity wrong-result (documented input = checkRankFR output, header line 10). The hand-built fixture (FRW without the -1 entries, FRwrows without dependent rows) hid both entries; the test is converted to the quarantine layout rather than strengthened. Reach: every call form with checkRankFR output that has a row rank deficiency; src callers of printFRdependencies: none. For the lead (checkRankFR is BLOCKED and untested; FR-012 does not apply but the finding matters for its future test): checkRankFR errors at line 541 for every input unless a solver named 'gurobi5' exists, and its FRwrows (line 641) contradicts its own header ('independent rows that dependent rows depend on').
confirmed_by: lead (review T027/T028; on real checkRankFR output it lists a dependent row as dependent on itself and among the independent rows; writer's MATLAB reproduction)
